BELIEF_STATE: UNDERSTANDING: Module responsibility: Add local user-defined command tools to the MCP surface without allowing them to replace built-in tools or produce unbounded output. Key data flows: - INPUT: JSON files under ~/.synapse/tools or SYNAPSE_TOOLS_DIR, MCP tools/list and tools/call requests, and syn tools CLI commands. - PROCESSING: Validate definitions, reject built-in override names, expose profile-visible schemas with _source metadata, interpolate scalar arguments into shell-escaped commands, enforce allowed_paths, run commands with timeout, and trim output by token budget. - OUTPUT: MCP tool definitions, MCP text results or JSON-RPC errors, CLI validation reports, and starter JSON templates. Critical invariants: - Built-in MCP names are protected from user override. - Dynamic tools are local-only command tools with timeout and output caps. - User tools appear after built-ins and do not weaken existing tools/list profiles. IMPLEMENTATION_STRATEGY: Approach: Keep dynamic tool loading in a separate MCP helper module and expose a narrow CLI authoring layer. Complexity_areas: safe command interpolation, path allowlist matching, test isolation for home-directory tools, and preserving tools/list token economy. Patterns_applied: explicit validation reports, source metadata, profile-aware filtering, bounded subprocess execution, and reuse of existing response trimming. VERIFICATION_INTENT: I expect the following to be true after my code runs: - cargo test mcp::user_tools and cli::tools_commands pass. - syn tools validate rejects built-in override names. - MCP tools/list can include user tools with _source=user metadata. - MCP tools/call can execute a user command tool with timeout and max output controls. RISKS_ACKNOWLEDGED: - User command tools intentionally execute local shell commands, so validation must stay conservative. - Dynamic tool schemas can increase tools/list size; existing terse/profile controls must remain effective.
